newsitem.title: USA: NYC Controller Hevesi audits city's capital needs.
newsitem.headline: NYC Controller Hevesi audits city's capital needs.

text.p: New York City Controller Alan Hevesi said Wednesday his office was conducting a lengthy audit of the city's capital needs.

Asked if the audit would suggest what programs might be cut, Hevesi replied, "What we might do is suggest what needs to be done. If your project doesn't make the list, you might draw your own conclusions."
Hevesi made the remarks at a beakfast sponsored by Crain's New York Business.

While applauding the Giuliani Administration's decision to use a revenue windfall to reduce budget gaps in the 1997 and 1998 fiscal years, Hevesi noted that New York City's debt service was well over 15 percent od revenues, which is an academic yardstick.
He said the cost would keep rising unless more was done to control spending. The city faces large future budget gaps, and debt service could rise above 20 percent, he said.
"It's another huge problem layered on top of us," Hevesi concluded.
